children: Brent crude pared earlier losses to trade around $106 a barrel on Friday as investors remained cautious over the prospects for a US-Iran agreement, given that previous negotiations have repeatedly appeared close to a breakthrough before collapsing.

US and Iranian negotiators have been exploring a phased arrangement that could reopen the Strait of Hormuz, potentially involving Tehran restoring access through the strategic waterway while Washington lifts its blockade of Iranian ports.

However, a White House official said President Donald Trump remained open to talks but maintained that the US was under no pressure to negotiate, citing the strength of its sanctions campaign and blockade.
Brent crude remained more than 2% higher for the week, reflecting continued supply concerns linked to the conflict.

title: Brent Crude Pares Losses
